clauses.reason: The lead prescribes the regulations governing the furnishing of clothing in kind or cash allowances to enlisted personnel of the four services. It continues until the sunset in the closing paragraph, June 30, 1949; the end source is the order's own text.

Section A lists the clothing in kind or cash allowances to which enlisted men are entitled, in tables that the OCR text breaks into fragments. It continues until the closing paragraph's sunset on June 30, 1949. Executive Order 10023, signed December 20, 1948 and effective as of December 1, 1948, adds a new subsection 11 to Section A (a cash allowance not to exceed $80.00 for the full dress uniform) for members of the United States Navy Band; under the owner ruling on amendments this is a later event and the clause continues, amended, until the order ends.

Section B governs when the cash clothing allowances are payable, including for reenlisted, recalled and transferred men. It continues until the closing paragraph's sunset on June 30, 1949. Executive Order 10023, signed December 20, 1948 and effective as of December 1, 1948, adds a new subsection 8 to Section B (who is paid the Navy Band allowance, that it is paid once in a period of continuous active duty, and on whose order) for members of the United States Navy Band; under the owner ruling on amendments this is a later event and the clause continues, amended, until the order ends.
Section C governs the quarterly maintenance allowance. It continues until the closing paragraph's sunset on June 30, 1949.

The closing paragraph supersedes Executive Orders No. 9744B, No. 9785 and No. 9869, makes the order effective as of July 1, 1948 and provides that it shall “continue in effect for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1949”. The supersession was performed on the effective date, July 1, 1948, and the effective-date statement was spent then; the duration command ends on June 30, 1949, so the clause as a whole ends on that date (inclusive; the exclusive reading would end it when that day begins). The end source is the order's own text.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 9984 (13 FR 4437 (Federal Register of August 3, 1948)) was signed July 31, 1948. Its held Federal Register text prints the order number, the title and the signing date. It prescribes regulations on clothing in kind or cash allowances in lieu of clothing for enlisted personnel of the Navy, Coast Guard, Naval Reserve and Coast Guard Reserve: Section A lists the allowances, Section B governs when the cash allowances are paid, Section C governs the quarterly maintenance allowance, and the closing paragraph supersedes Executive Order No. 9744B, No. 9785 and No. 9869, makes the order effective as of July 1, 1948 and provides that it shall “continue in effect for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1949”. On 2026-10-14 every clause is terminated by that own-terms sunset, June 30, 1949. The dossier's forty clause fragments come from the OCR of the allowance tables and are replaced by five operative pieces: the lead, Sections A, B and C, and the closing paragraph. The searches for an earlier end found one later event, Executive Order 10023 (signed December 20, 1948, effective as of December 1, 1948), which adds subsection 11 to Section A and subsection 8 to Section B for members of the Navy Band; it is an amendment and not an end. A held-text search for citations of this order, with and without a trailing footnote digit, found only Executive Order 10023 and its copies and the Federal Register page of August 3, 1948. The Federal Register disposition-note search lists the one hit (Executive Order 10023); the U.S. Code and eCFR searches report no hit.
